## Motivation

## Theorem and Proof

::: {#thm-geometric-series}
## Geometric Series

For any $r \neq 1$ and positive integer $n$,

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} r^k
=
\frac{1-r^n}{1-r}.
$$
:::

::: {.proof}
Let

$$
S = 1+r+r^2+\cdots+r^{n-1}.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $r$ gives

$$
rS = r+r^2+\cdots+r^n.
$$

Subtracting,

$$
(1-r)S = 1-r^n.
$$

Since $r\neq 1$, we obtain

$$
S = \frac{1-r^n}{1-r}.
$$

This completes the proof.
:::

As established in @thm-geometric-series,
the finite geometric series has a closed-form
expression.
